findings.heading: New factory
findings.proposition: The English says the 'scripts' folder holds other R scripts that are SOURCED BY the Rmd scripts; the Russian reverses the direction and says the scripts there CALL your Rmd scripts ('которые вызывают ваши скрипты Rmd').
findings.reader_consequence: A Russian reader inverts the dependency of the factory layout: they will expect the .R files in 'scripts' to drive the reports, and so will not put helper code there to be sourced from inside an Rmd, which is the pattern the rest of the chapter (and the 'Scripts' section) relies on.

findings.heading: Compile from sub-folder
findings.proposition: The English states that giving the subfolder name with a trailing slash to `reports = ` compiles ALL Rmd reports in that subfolder; the Russian drops 'all' and says only that it compiles Rmd reports in the subfolder.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader misses the whole point of the trailing-slash form, which is batch compilation of a folder, and may keep listing reports one by one instead of using `compile_reports(reports = "for_partners/")`.

findings.heading: Compile by number
findings.proposition: The English imposes a requirement on the user ('The numbers MUST align with the order the reports appear when you run `list_reports()`'); the Russian states it as a fact about the software ('Номера будут соответствовать порядку' — the numbers WILL correspond to the order).
findings.reader_consequence: The reader treats the numbering as something the package guarantees rather than something they must check, so they will pass `reports = c(2, 4)` without first running `list_reports()` and can compile the wrong reports.

findings.heading: New factory
findings.proposition: The English says the .gitignore file is created IN CASE you link the project to a Github repository (a conditional convenience); the Russian says it was created IN ORDER TO link your R project to a Github repository ('чтобы связать ваш проект R с репозиторием Github').
findings.reader_consequence: The reader may believe the generated .gitignore itself establishes the link to Github, and so will not perform the actual repository setup described in the Version control chapter.

findings.heading: New factory
findings.proposition: The English specifies that the 'report_sources' folder holds your R MARKDOWN scripts; the Russian says only 'ваши скрипты' (your scripts), dropping the R Markdown qualifier.
findings.reader_consequence: The distinction between 'report_sources' (Rmd report scripts) and 'scripts' (other .R files) is blurred, so the reader may save plain .R files into 'report_sources', where `compile_reports()` and `list_reports()` do not treat them as reports.

findings.heading: Create a report
findings.proposition: The English carries a working cross-reference to the Import and export chapter ('[Import and export](importing.qmd)'); the Russian keeps only the bracketed label '[Импорт и экспорт]' with no link target.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader cannot follow the pointer to the Import and export chapter for details on the **here** filepath idiom, and sees a stray bracketed phrase rendered as literal text instead of a link.

findings.heading: Parameterization
findings.proposition: The English carries a working cross-reference to the R Markdown reports chapter ('[Reports with R Markdown](rmarkdown.qmd)'); the Russian keeps only the bracketed label '[Отчеты с помощью R Markdown]' with no link target.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader cannot reach the chapter that explains how report parameters are declared in the YAML header, which is the prerequisite for using the `params = ` argument shown in the chunk below.

findings.heading: Scripts
findings.proposition: The English links to the R Markdown chapter ('[R Markdown](rmarkdown.qmd)') for tips on structuring code across several files; the Russian writes a reference-style link '[R Markdown][Отчеты с помощью R Markdown]' with no matching link definition anywhere in the file, so no target exists.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader cannot reach the guidance on splitting code across files, and the text renders as unresolved bracket syntax rather than a usable link.
